This post combines Python and R code demonstrations in Quarto.

Data source: https://github.com/mcnakhaee/palmerpenguins

## Python Section

```{python}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
import pandas as pd
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

penguins = load_penguins()
penguins.head()
```

```{python}
#| label: fig-penguin-mass-python-mixed
#| fig-cap: "Mean Body Mass by Sex and Island (Python)."
df_py = penguins.groupby(['sex', 'island']).agg({'body_mass_g': 'mean'})
ax = df_py.unstack()['body_mass_g'].plot(kind='bar', figsize=(8, 5))
plt.title("Mean Body Mass by Sex and Island (Python)")
plt.ylabel("Mean Body Mass (g)")
plt.xlabel("Sex")
plt.xticks(rotation=0) # Rotate x-axis labels for better readability
plt.legend(title="Island")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```








## R Section

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(palmerpenguins)
library(tidyverse)
```

```{r}
data("penguins")
glimpse(penguins)
```

```{r}
df_r <- penguins |>
    drop_na() |>
    group_by(sex, island) |>
    summarize(mean_mass = mean(body_mass_g, na.rm = TRUE))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-penguin-mass-r-mixed
#| fig-cap: "Mean Body Mass by Island & Sex (R)."

ggplot(df_r, aes(x = sex, y = mean_mass, fill = island)) +
    geom_col(position = "dodge", alpha = 0.85) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
    labs(
        title = "Mean Body Mass by Island & Sex (R)",
        x = "Island",
        y = "Mean Body Mass (g)",
        fill = "Sex"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()
```
